headline: Local Cricket Fan Decides To Maintain 223-Run Lead In Personal Life To Mirror Match Performance
body:
Anuj Deshmukh, a 28-year-old freelance accountant from Indiranagar, has officially declared his household 'in a chase' after a star batsman’s recent 223-run masterpiece. Deshmukh has instructed his family to treat all domestic milestones as 'runs,' requiring him to maintain a personal margin of exactly 223 points over his wife in every activity, including grocery shopping speed, dish-washing velocity, and the number of unread WhatsApp notifications.

'The psychology of the chase is simple, really,' said Deshmukh, who was seen pacing his living room wearing his batting pads while holding a spatula. 'If our national team can overhaul an impossible target because one man decided to bat like he’s playing against ghosts, then surely I can clear my pending household chores with the same ruthless efficiency. I’ve currently calculated that I am 223 items of laundry ahead of the rest of the family, which makes me feel incredibly secure.'

His wife, Meera, confirmed that the domestic situation has become increasingly difficult to manage. 'He wouldn’t let me leave for work this morning until I acknowledged that he had scored a boundary by successfully assembling a flat-pack shelf in under four minutes,' she explained. 'I’m just hoping the series ends soon so he can go back to being a normal person who occasionally forgets to turn off the lights instead of a man who thinks every light switch is a tactical review request.'
caption: Domestic life is now officially a sport. How many runs are you currently behind in your own household chase? #CricketFever #DomesticCricket #WorkLifeBalance (satire)
